summary.value: The purpose of ELIXIR-STEERS is to build capacity for large-scale, cross-border data analysis and for this capacity to be embedded across member states. ELIXIR-STEERS directly benefit Europe’s life scientists by allowing software and workflows to meet requirements of those using them in national centres. A ‘robust, reproducible and green’ approach to software and workflow provision will ensure that scientists have access to high quality, energy-efficient analysis tools. The project will also develop the crediting and recognition systems for software, supporting improvements to research assessment frameworks.

summary.value: Now it is transitioning to a sustainable framework for enabling real-world data integration and reuse by promoting and supporting interoperability, data management and FAIR principles. The strategy centres on "The 3 Ps": Products, Processes, and Practices. Products entail mapping and coordinating FAIR resources, minimising duplication, and enhancing user experience. Processes align products with user needs, ELIXIR Nodes, and global partners. Practices convert insights into actionable guidance, empowering users through the connection and use of diverse resources.

summary.value: The Plant Sciences Community is an interdisciplinary group of researchers with diverse backgrounds from computer science to different fields of plant biology. We answer the needs of both bioinformaticians and plant biologists. The Community objective is to develop an infrastructure supporting the integration and linking of different plant data types. These data types range from phenomics and genomics to transcriptomics, metabolomics, modelling and bibliographic data. The underlying scientific use cases encompass genetics and genomics approaches in plant sciences, with an extension of the scope towards system biology. The Community aims at promoting tools, databases, standards and best practices for plant research.

summary.value: The Plant Sciences Community is an interdisciplinary group of researchers with diverse backgrounds from computer science to different fields of plant biology. We answer the needs of both bioinformaticians and plant biologists. The Community objective is to develop an infrastructure supporting the integration and linking of different plant data types. These data types range from phenomics and genomics to transcriptomics, metabolomics, modelling and bibliographic data. The underlying scientific use cases encompass genetics and genomics approaches in plant sciences, with an extension of the scope towards system biology. The Community aims at promoting tools, databases, standards and best practices for plant research.

summary.value: The purpose of ELIXIR-STEERS is to build capacity for large-scale, cross-border data analysis and for this capacity to be embedded across member states. ELIXIR-STEERS directly benefit Europe’s life scientists by allowing software and workflows to meet requirements of those using them in national centres. A ‘robust, reproducible and green’ approach to software and workflow provision will ensure that scientists have access to high quality, energy-efficient analysis tools. The project will also develop the crediting and recognition systems for software, supporting improvements to research assessment frameworks.

summary.value: The AI Ecosystem Focus Group brings together experts from ELIXIR’s Nodes to address growing challenges within the scientific AI/ML field, particularly the need for harmonisation in AI/ML infrastructure. summary.value: As a research infrastructure, ELIXIR relies upon a diverse range of roles, such as trainers, data stewards, project managers, software engineers, developers, community managers. However, careers within research infrastructure remain poorly defined. By clarifying the career options within a research infrastructure, we aim to promote interest in these roles to support the career development of researchers beyond the traditional academic paths of, for example, Principal Investigators. As well as supporting the research community by recognising infrastructure career paths, this Focus Group will actively contribute to ELIXIR's commitment to diversity and inclusion within the research ecosystem.

summary.value: This project focuses on improving Galaxy’s data management features to provide additional provenance information and improve the integration of Galaxy in the existing data management ecosystem. Among the goals, we aim to make the Galaxy Data Libraries more scalable and further improve the reusability features of the platform by metadata enrichment. The Galaxy metadata system will be extended to enable the export of analysis records together with their provenance to relevant ELIXIR Core Data Resources and registries (e.g. WorkflowHub). A strong focus is put on the integration of EGA, FAIRtracks, and the GA4GH Beacon network into Galaxy to support analyses of human data. Therefore, support for user-level encrypted data processing is also added to allow for the analysis of sensitive data. To this end, we include an encryption layer in the Pulsar network and enhance performance by increasing the data locality of distributed Galaxy analyses through a prototype data caching network.

While sequencing costs have declined, leading to an influx of data for agriculturally important species like wheat, rice and potato, researchers currently struggle with quantifying the completeness of assemblies and gene annotations. E-PAN aims to streamline these efforts by developing effective standards, computational pipelines and tutorials for quality control (QC) and data sharing. The project will also evaluate and integrate advanced visualisation and data-mining modules into existing ELIXIR platforms, such as PLAZA/FRINGE, BARLEX and KnetMiner. Ultimately, these concerted efforts will facilitate the development of more resilient cultivars by making genomic diversity easier to interpret and share.

summary.value: Despite exponential growth in data production, biodiversity datasets lack consistent FAIR evaluations tailored to their domain-specific needs. BioDiv-FAIR-Checker will build on the ELIXIR-developed FAIR-Checker generic assessment tool to design and implement biodiversity-domain-tailored evaluation metrics with remediation hints. In alignment with the priorities of the ELIXIR Biodiversity Community and the activities of the ELIXIR Platforms, the project will pilot the service on genomics data (ENA), collections specimen digital objects (DiSSCo) and ecological observations datasets (eLTER, GBIF). Targeted to biodiversity datasets, but with potential applications to the agriculture/aquaculture and pathogens domains, the project will deliver BFSP-relevant services that advance data FAIRification and enhance standards.

summary.value: The E-PAN project addresses the lack of standardisation and tools for the integration and exploration of plant pan-genomes. While sequencing costs have declined, leading to an influx of data for agriculturally important species like wheat, rice and potato, researchers currently struggle with quantifying the completeness of assemblies and gene annotations. E-PAN aims to streamline these efforts by developing effective standards, computational pipelines and tutorials for quality control (QC) and data sharing. The project will also evaluate and integrate advanced visualisation and data-mining modules into existing ELIXIR platforms, such as PLAZA/FRINGE, BARLEX and KnetMiner. Ultimately, these concerted efforts will facilitate the development of more resilient cultivars by making genomic diversity easier to interpret and share.

summary.value: KYBELE aims to develop an AI-powered, FAIR-compliant system to unlock biodiversity knowledge from genomic and ecological literature repositories (PMC, BHL, Zenodo). By harvesting species data, traits and habitats from BOLD and annotating BiodiversityPMC with domain vocabularies, the project creates structured resources for reuse. Generative LLMs, fine-tuned through LoRA and distillation, will enable interactive literature exploration via a containerised chatbox deployed jointly across the ELIXIR and LifeWatch ERIC portfolios. Through dissemination, training and integration with existing infrastructure, KYBELE delivers sustainable services that strengthen ELIXIR’s biodiversity portfolio, support the BFSP Priority Area and empower researchers with innovative tools and datasets to advance scientific discovery.

summary.value: Documented regulatory interactions between Transcription Factors (TFs) and target genes (TGs) form a crucial resource for biological network building. The ExTRI text mining project yielded about 54,000 sentences from literature that proposedly describe a TF-TG interaction, linked to database identifiers. This corpus is now a compelling target for a community curation effort, which will be performed by dedicated curators in this project, and modelers potentially contributing via Cytoscape. To make this large-scale effort possible, we will combine the intuitive and flexible curation tool VSM (Visual Syntax Method), with automated NLP (Natural Language Processing) assistance, into a community curation app. Premarked ExTRI sentences will be shown in their abstract, along with NLP annotations provided by Europe-PMC's API, to help curators formalize knowledge into a form suitable for computational analysis. The new web app will be designed for reusability, guided by professional curation partners, and evaluated for effect on curator performance.

summary.value: The aim of this implementation study is to provide a stable infrastructure for unifying software containers solutions within ELIXIR. This infrastructure will provide an access point for end-users to find, generate, store, monitor, and even benchmark software containers solutions. Hardware infrastructure will be provided by an ELIXIR Node from the ELIXIR Compute Platform for software containers deployment while ELIXIR Spain will provide the backup system using EUDAT protocols and infrastructures. In the long-term this registry could become a relying service to the ELIXIR AAI allowing infrastructures to manage users accounts.

The overall goal is to provide secure, standardized, documented and interoperable services under the framework of the European Genome-phenome Archive (EGA). This three year plan includes a structured roadmap for ELIXIR Nodes to join the EGA federated network by providing the necessary technical, logistical, and training coordination across the network.

summary.value: Here we propose a set of meetings and working groups between the resources ChEBI (EMBL-EBI) and Rhea (SIB), with the aim of streamlining the link between chemicals (ChEBI), reactions (Rhea) and pathways (Reactome) and to provide guidelines on the representation of chemical entities to the metabolic modelling community. We anticipate that the development of closer interactions and working relationships between core staff from the different resources during the course of this project will enable further streamlining and increased levels of interoperability between these ELIXIR resources. It will lead to a greater degree of understanding of the underlying workflows of each resource and to more efficient coordination of their development.

summary.value: Europe’s life sciences produce vast amounts of data, much of it stored in national or institutional centres. To help researchers find, access, and analyse this distributed data, the EU-funded ELIXIR-STEERS project aims to strengthen ELIXIR (Europe’s landmark infrastructure for life science data). The project will build capacity for large-scale, cross-border data analysis. This will ensure that software and workflows meet the needs of scientists working in national centres. A focus on robust, reproducible, and energy-efficient tools will support high-quality, greener research. ELIXIR-STEERS will also improve training and operational excellence across ELIXIR Nodes, expanding membership to new countries. Global collaborations, combined with better software recognition, will support a sustainable future for Europe’s life science data ecosystem.

summary.value: Following prioritisation of European research infrastructures by ESFRI, the ELIXIR-EXCELERATE project (2015-2019) was awarded to accelerate the construction of ELIXIR. ELIXIR-EXCELERATE developed ELIXIR’s service platforms, established infrastructure operation and internal processes, and launched the ELIXIR Innovation and SME programme. The project was driven by use cases from four research communities: marine metagenomics, plant sciences, rare disease and human genomics. Thus, ELIXIR-EXCELERATE supported the early exploitation of infrastructure services by user communities across the life sciences.

It builds upon the groundwork laid by the Beyond 1 Million Genomes (B1MG) project and aims to realize the vision of the 1+Million Genomes (1+MG) initiative. GDI focuses on integrating data from national databases, emphasizing areas such as the Genome of Europe, cancer, and infectious diseases. To ensure data privacy and compliance with European and national laws, the infrastructure provides controlled access to approved clinicians, researchers, and policymakers, while non-sensitive, aggregated data will be openly discoverable through tools like the European Genome Dashboard.
